spec.expr: resets(proxmox_node_uptime{node=~"$node"}[$__interval]) > 0
resets(proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node"}[$__interval]) > 0

spec.description: Capacity, right-sizing, and topology across the Proxmox fleet. Answers what to resize and what to buy, rather than what is broken right now.

spec.title: vCPU Commitment
spec.description: Allocated vCPU across running guests as a share of physical cores. Above 100% is overcommit, which is normal and healthy until the guests actually want the CPU at the same time -- compare with the pressure panels on the Guests dashboard.

spec.expr: sum(proxmox_vm_cpus{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0) / on () sum(proxmox_node_cpustat_cpus{node=~"$node"}) * 100

spec.title: RAM Commitment
spec.description: Allocated guest RAM as a share of host RAM. Unlike vCPU this one bites: memory cannot be time-sliced, so sustained values above 100% mean the host is relying on ballooning or is genuinely oversubscribed.

spec.expr: sum(proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0) / on () sum(proxmox_node_memory_memtotal{node=~"$node"}) * 100

spec.title: Reclaimable RAM
spec.description: Allocated minus actually used, summed across running guests. This is the headroom you could hand back by right-sizing -- not free host memory, which is on the Node Operations dashboard.

spec.expr: sum(proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0) - sum(proxmox_vm_mem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0)

spec.title: Disk Commitment
spec.description: Provisioned guest disk against total storage capacity. Thin-provisioned storage makes values above 100% legitimate; it is the trend that matters.

spec.expr: sum(proxmox_vm_maxdisk{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"}) / on () sum(proxmox_storage_total{node=~"$node", storage=~"$storage"}) * 100

spec.title: Right-sizing Quadrant
spec.description: Every running guest placed by how much of its OWN allocation it uses. Bottom-left is over-provisioned and safe to shrink; top-right is at its ceiling and should grow. Bubble size is allocated RAM, so a large bubble in the bottom-left is the most wasted capacity in the fleet. Hover for the guest name.

spec.expr: sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_cpu{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0)
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_mem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} / proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})

spec.title: Right-sizing Detail
spec.description: Allocated against actual, per guest. 'vCPU used' is the guest's CPU fraction times its vCPU count, so it is directly comparable to the vCPU column. 'Reclaimable' is allocated minus used RAM -- the single most useful number here. Click a row to open that guest.

spec.expr: sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_cpus{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_cpu{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} * proxmox_vm_cpus{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_mem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} - proxmox_vm_mem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_disk{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} / proxmox_vm_maxdisk{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})

spec.title: Per-Guest Network (host-side)
spec.description: Measured on the host's veth/tap interfaces rather than reported by the guest, so it also covers guests with no agent. Polarity is inverted across the boundary: what the NODE transmits is what the GUEST receives. Positive is into the guest.

spec.expr: sum by (vmid) (label_replace(rate(proxmox_node_network_transmit_total{node=~"$node", device=~"(tap|veth|fw)[a-z0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]), "vmid", "$1", "device", "(?:tap|veth|fw)(\\d+)i\\d+"))
-1 * sum by (vmid) (label_replace(rate(proxmox_node_network_receive_total{node=~"$node", device=~"(tap|veth|fw)[a-z0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]), "vmid", "$1", "device", "(?:tap|veth|fw)(\\d+)i\\d+"))

spec.title: Wire Share by Guest
spec.description: Total bidirectional throughput per guest right now, attributed from the host-side interface name. The quick read when you only want to know who is loudest on the wire.

spec.expr: sum by (vmid) (label_replace(rate(proxmox_node_network_transmit_total{node=~"$node", device=~"(tap|veth|fw)[a-z0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]), "vmid", "$1", "device", "(?:tap|veth|fw)(\\d+)i\\d+")) + on (vmid) sum by (vmid) (label_replace(rate(proxmox_node_network_receive_total{node=~"$node", device=~"(tap|veth|fw)[a-z0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]), "vmid", "$1", "device", "(?:tap|veth|fw)(\\d+)i\\d+"))
sum by (vmid, name, type) (proxmox_vm_cpus{node=~"$node"}) * 0 + 1

spec.title: Guest Reachability
spec.description: Derived from uptime, because Proxmox emits no status metric and no up{} series. A gap means the guest stopped reporting entirely, which is different from reporting zero -- see the Guests dashboard for that distinction.

spec.expr: clamp_max(proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"}, 1)

spec.title: Fleet CPU Distribution
spec.description: How the fleet's per-guest CPU usage is DISTRIBUTED over time, not its total. A single bright band low down is a healthy idle fleet; a band that climbs, or splits, means load is concentrating in a few guests. Proxmox emits no histograms, so Grafana buckets the raw values.

spec.expr: proxmox_vm_cpu{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0

spec.title: Fleet Memory Distribution
spec.description: Same idea for memory: each guest as a fraction of its own allocation. Guests pinned near 1.0 are the ones that will start swapping or OOM first.

spec.expr: sum by (vmid) (proxmox_vm_mem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0) / sum by (vmid) (proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})

spec.title: Pressure Stall (CPU / IO / memory, full)
spec.description: 'full' pressure means EVERY runnable task in the guest was stalled on that resource. Unlike utilisation it does not saturate at 100%, so it is the earliest honest signal that a guest is undersized. Any sustained non-zero value here is worth acting on.

spec.expr: sum by (vmid) (proxmox_vm_pressurecpufull{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0)
sum by (vmid) (proxmox_vm_pressureiofull{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0)
sum by (vmid) (proxmox_vm_pressurememoryfull{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0)

spec.title: Storage Runway
spec.description: Days until full at the growth rate observed across the CURRENT time range -- widen the range for a steadier estimate. `> 0` is a filter, not a clamp: storage that is flat or shrinking drops out of the result entirely rather than being divided by a tiny floor and drawn as a reassuring full-length bar.

spec.expr: sum by (storage) (proxmox_storage_avail{node=~"$node", storage=~"$storage"}) / (sum by (storage) (deriv(proxmox_storage_used{node=~"$node", storage=~"$storage"}[$__range])) > 0) / 86400

defaults.noValue: Flat or shrinking — no runway to project

spec.title: Storage Growth Rate
spec.description: Bytes per second of net growth per storage. Negative means space is being freed. This is the number the runway projection divides by, shown so you can judge whether the projection is trustworthy.

spec.expr: sum by (storage) (deriv(proxmox_storage_used{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Host RAM Headroom
spec.description: Available rather than free: it includes reclaimable page cache and the shrinkable part of the ZFS ARC, which is what the kernel would actually hand to a new guest.

spec.expr: sum(proxmox_node_memory_memavailable{node=~"$node"}) / sum(proxmox_node_memory_memtotal{node=~"$node"}) * 100

spec.title: Physical Core Headroom
spec.description: Idle share of physical CPU. Read together with vCPU Commitment on the first tab: high commitment plus high headroom is a well-packed host, high commitment plus low headroom is contention.

spec.expr: (1 - sum(proxmox_node_cpustat_cpu{node=~"$node"})) * 100

spec.title: Hypervisor Efficiency
spec.description: Share of BUSY host CPU actually spent executing guest code. The remainder is host services, the hypervisor itself, and I/O handling. Proxmox reports `guest` as its own /proc/stat mode rather than nesting it inside `user`, which is what makes this ratio computable at all. A number that falls while guest load is steady means overhead is growing.

spec.expr: sum(rate(proxmox_node_cpustat_guest_total{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(proxmox_node_cpustat_used{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])) * 100

spec.title: Unattributed Host RAM
spec.description: Host memory that is neither guest RAM nor ZFS ARC: Proxmox services, kernel structures, page tables, and the per-VM QEMU process overhead. It is the part of the memory bill nobody itemises, and it grows with guest count rather than with guest size.

spec.expr: clamp_min(sum(proxmox_node_memory_memused{node=~"$node"}) - sum(proxmox_vm_mem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0) - sum(proxmox_node_memory_arcsize{node=~"$node"}), 0)

spec.title: Memory Accounting
spec.description: Where the host's RAM actually went. The four bands sum to memtotal by construction: guest RAM, the ZFS ARC, everything else that is in use, and what is left. 'host + hypervisor' is a residual, so it absorbs any accounting error as well as real overhead -- treat a sudden jump as a question, not a fact. Watch the ARC band expand into free memory and contract again under pressure.

spec.expr: sum(proxmox_vm_mem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0)
sum(proxmox_node_memory_arcsize{node=~"$node"})

clamp_min(sum(proxmox_node_memory_memused{node=~"$node"}) - sum(proxmox_vm_mem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0) - sum(proxmox_node_memory_arcsize{node=~"$node"}), 0)
sum(proxmox_node_memory_memtotal{node=~"$node"}) - sum(proxmox_node_memory_memused{node=~"$node"})

spec.title: QEMU Memory Tax
spec.description: What each QEMU guest costs the host ON TOP of the RAM the guest itself sees: the emulator process, device models, and page tables. LXC containers have no such layer and report nothing here. This is the per-guest slice of 'Unattributed Host RAM' above, and it is why guest count -- not just guest size -- drives host memory.

spec.expr: proxmox_vm_memhost{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} - proxmox_vm_mem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"}

defaults.noValue: No QEMU guests reporting host-side memory

spec.title: Guest Agent Freshness
spec.description: How recently each QEMU balloon driver last reported, encoded as a state. A wedged guest agent stops updating while the VM keeps running and keeps looking healthy everywhere else -- every other guest metric comes from the host and carries on regardless. This is the only panel that catches it. `> bool` turns each threshold into 0/1 so the two comparisons add up to a state, rather than filtering series out.

spec.expr: (time() - proxmox_vm_ballooninfo_last_update{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > bool 60) + (time() - proxmox_vm_ballooninfo_last_update{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > bool 300)

spec.title: Guest Availability
spec.description: Fraction of the selected time range each guest was reporting a non-zero uptime, sampled every 5 minutes. Because uptime is the only running-state signal Proxmox emits, this cannot distinguish a stopped guest from a template -- but across a long range it is a fair availability figure, and the current uptime column tells you whether a low score is historical or happening now.

spec.expr: sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (avg_over_time(clamp_max(proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"}, 1)[$__range:5m]))
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})

spec.title: Proxmox VE · Fleet Intelligence
